subsystems.name: Motion coupling
subsystems.role: converts body movement into relative motion inside the device.

subsystems.name: Power conditioning
subsystems.role: turns the ragged, low-voltage output into something a circuit can use.

subsystems.name: Energy storage
subsystems.role: buffers power so the load sees a steady supply.

subsystems.name: Load and management
subsystems.role: spends the harvested energy where it matters.

buildSteps.title: Measure the motion
buildSteps.detail: Accelerometers record how fast and how forcefully the target body part moves — a heel strikes at roughly 1–2 steps per second, a wrist swings at similar low frequencies.

buildSteps.title: Design the coupling
buildSteps.detail: Because human motion is slow and irregular, resonant spring-mass harvesters are hard to tune. Most working designs use an eccentric weighted rotor (as in a self-winding watch) or magnetic plucking that snaps a piezoelectric beam at a higher, more efficient frequency.

buildSteps.title: Choose the transducer
buildSteps.detail: Electromagnetic coils give more power for a given volume at watch-and-shoe scale; piezoelectric beams suit very small MEMS devices; electrostatic types need an external pre-charge, which limits them.

buildSteps.title: Optimise magnetics
buildSteps.detail: Magnet grade, air gap, pole geometry and coil turns are tuned together, since induced voltage scales with the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate
buildSteps.detail: Coils are wound and potted, magnets and rotors are assembled to tight tolerances, and the mechanism is sealed against sweat, dust and shock.

buildSteps.title: Condition the power
buildSteps.detail: A rectifier converts the alternating output to DC; a switched converter steps it to the voltage the load needs, and a cold-start circuit lets the device boot from a completely empty storage capacitor.

buildSteps.title: Store and test
buildSteps.detail: A supercapacitor or thin-film cell smooths the bursts, and the whole unit is cycled on a shaker rig or a walking volunteer to confirm it keeps the load alive.

prerequisites.why: neodymium-iron-boron magnets make small harvesters possible at all.
microcontrollers and radios that run on microwatts are what make harvesting worthwhile.
they extract usable power from millivolt-level inputs and start up from cold.
needed to pack a transducer into a wristwatch-sized volume.
thin-film batteries and supercapacitors absorb intermittent bursts.

pathway.unlocks: small consumer devices that never need a battery change.

pathway.milestone: wearable harvesters paired with duty-cycled radios
pathway.unlocks: body sensors for fitness and health that need no charging at all.
power for medical monitors and location beacons worn all day.

pathway.unlocks: genuinely battery-free wearables and industrial sensors — though motion alone will never charge a phone at useful speed.
